claims.text: PostgreSQL writes every change to the write-ahead log before the data files are changed; replaying the WAL from a known starting point (a checkpoint or base backup) redoes every change made since.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 28.3 Write-Ahead Logging (WAL); 25.3 Continuous Archiving and Point-in-Time Recovery (intro)

claims.text: pg_basebackup takes a base backup of a running PostgreSQL server; it always copies the whole server (every database), never a single database.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: pg_basebackup Description ('backups are always taken of the entire database cluster')

claims.text: With archive_mode on, the server runs archive_command for each completed WAL segment (file); in the command %p is replaced by the segment's path and %f by its file name.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.3.1 Setting Up WAL Archiving; 19.5.3 Archiving (archive_mode, archive_command)

claims.text: PITR starts a server from a base backup and replays archived WAL (fetched by restore_command, with recovery.signal present) up to recovery_target_time; transactions committed after the target are not applied.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.3.5 Recovering Using a Continuous Archive Backup; 19.5.5 Recovery Target (recovery_target_time, recovery_target_inclusive)

claims.text: Recovery from a base backup and archived WAL restores the whole server, so every database on it returns to the same moment; one database cannot be recovered to a different time on its own.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.3 Continuous Archiving (works on the entire cluster); pg_basebackup Description

claims.text: Changes in a WAL segment not yet completed and archived exist only on the live server; with archiving, the data lost with the server is the WAL not yet archived.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.3.1 Setting Up WAL Archiving (archive_command only invoked on completed segments; archive_timeout paragraph)

claims.text: If archive_command exits non-zero, PostgreSQL treats archiving as failed, retries the same segment periodically, and does not remove or recycle the segment until it is archived. test ! -f refuses to overwrite an existing archive file.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.3.1 Setting Up WAL Archiving ('zero exit status if and only if it succeeds'; 'will not be removed or recycled'; test ! -f example)

claims.text: archive_timeout: when greater than zero, the server switches to a new WAL segment once that many seconds have elapsed since the last switch and there has been database activity, so a partly filled segment gets archived; db sets it to 60.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 19.5.3 Archiving (archive_timeout); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml:87

claims.text: With archive_timeout=60 on a quiet server, if db's own files are lost while the archive survives, the WAL not yet archived covers at most about a minute of changes; losing the machine that also holds wal-archive is not covered.
claims.source_hint: Follows from claim 8; course definition of RPO (devops.l3.rpo-and-rto)

claims.text: docker-compose.yml lines 74-87 (stage-3) run db with archive_mode=on, an archive_command that compresses each segment with gzip into /wal-archive/%f.gz (the wal-archive volume, a local Docker volume on the same machine), and archive_timeout=60.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml:74-87, 100, 653

claims.text: base-backup.sh (outside the excerpts) runs pg_basebackup against db into /backups/base.new, then replaces /backups/base with it, keeping only the newest base backup.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/base-backup.sh:12-17

claims.text: pg_switch_wal() forces a switch to a new WAL file, so the current segment is completed and can be archived; pg_walfile_name gives that segment's file name; pg_stat_archiver.last_archived_wal reports the name of the last segment archived successfully.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 9.28.3 Backup Control Functions (pg_switch_wal, pg_walfile_name); 27.2 pg_stat_archiver view

claims.text: pitr.sh lines 34-58 delete order 3's items, switch and wait for the segment to be archived, recreate db-pitr (profile pitr) with RECOVERY_TARGET_TIME=$target, and wait until pg_get_wal_replay_pause_state() returns paused, else print 'db-pitr did not reach recovery_target_time' and exit 1.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/pitr.sh:34-58

claims.text: Outside the excerpt, pitr.sh: on_db/on_pitr run psql on db/db-pitr, value prints a query's result from db (8-10); runs base-backup.sh if none exists (13-16); $target = clock_timestamp() a second before the DELETE (29-31); COPY rows back (65-68).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/devops/pitr.sh:8-16, 29-31, 61-68; outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/pitr.txt (0 rows on db, 2 on db-pitr, COPY 2)

claims.text: db-pitr: separate container, profile pitr, backups and wal-archive mounted read-only; db keeps running. start.sh unpacks the base backup only into an empty data dir, then sets recovery_target_time and recovery_target_action=pause, so it pauses read-only at the target.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml:612-630; db/pitr/start.sh; PostgreSQL 17 docs 19.5.5 recovery_target_action (pause), 26.4 Hot Standby

claims.text: A read replica applies every change streamed from the primary, a mistaken DELETE included, so it holds the newest data, not an earlier moment.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 26.2 Log-Shipping Standby Servers / 26.2.5 Streaming Replication

claims.text: A base backup on its own restores the server only as of (the end of) the backup; reaching any later moment requires the archived WAL from the backup's start onward, and replay cannot go past the first missing segment.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 25.3 Continuous Archiving (need a continuous sequence of archived WAL files extending back to the base backup); 25.3.5

claims.text: Recovery to a target stops between committed transactions: a transaction is applied only if it committed before the target, so one not yet committed at that moment is left out entirely, never half applied.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 19.5.5 Recovery Target (stop point defined by transaction commit; recovery_target_inclusive)

claims.text: When a mistake touches only some rows, recovering into a separate server and copying those rows back is preferable to replacing the live server, if other databases and tables have been written since the target moment.
claims.source_hint: Design choice of pitr.sh (docker-compose.yml:612-615 comment); follows from claim 5

claims.text: The db server hosts donhang, donhang_payments and keycloak (among others), so db-pitr recovers all of them to the same moment.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 docker-compose.yml:351,367; db/databases.sql

claims.text: If a recovery target is configured but archive recovery ends before the target is reached, the server shuts down with a fatal error instead of pausing.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs: 19.5.6 Recovery Target (end of recovery before target)
